baseline.mode: vite development server, one Playwright worker and one browser process

candidate.mode: production preview, one shared local Chromium process, fresh context per test and fully parallel Playwright workers
candidate.workerRule: min(16, logical CPUs minus 2, one worker per 2 GiB), override with CODEVETTER_E2E_WORKERS

limitations: The baseline is one corrected exhaustive sample; the candidate is three serial exhaustive samples on one machine.
Maximum resident set size is command-level and does not sum every descendant process; the candidate peak is higher because the build and up to 16 isolated contexts overlap.
The result applies to CodeVetter's current 79-test Chromium corpus and does not predict another project's speedup.
Production-preview equivalence is guarded by the same exhaustive tests, but development-server-specific behavior remains covered by the existing direct Playwright command.
